newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MAN UTD WIN CHARITY SHIELD ON PENALTIES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MAN UTD WIN CHARITY SHIELD ON PENALTIES.

text.p: League champions Manchester United won English soccer's season-opening Charity Shield on penalties on Sunday after the game against FA Cup winners Chelsea ended 1-1.
Both goals in a scrappy and rather bad-tempered match came from headers following second half corners.

Unmarked striker Mark Hughes nodded Gianfranco Zola's cross down neatly at the far post in the 52nd minute to put Chelsea ahead but United defender Ronny Johnsen converted a lofted corner from Ryan Giggs five minutes later.
With the scores level at full time, Chelsea missed two penalties to give United a 4-2 shoot-out victory.

Frank Sinclair's shot was saved by Peter Schmeichel diving to his right and Roberto Di Matteo, who scored the fastest Wembley Cup final goal last May, blasted over the bar. Nicky Butt scored the winning spot kick for United, who retain the shield after beating Newcastle last season.
The Charity Shield played at Wembley is the traditional season curtain-raiser friendly between the league champions and F.A. Cup winners.
